items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Freddie 'Snake Hips' Taylor and I lived in the same hotel... I went to Freddie's room a few times... we called each other brother from then on

ctx.x: I had copied the first 8 measures of "I Found You In Maytime" the way I heard Freddie Jenkins play it when I had heard him with Edgar Hayes in Kentucky. It was a phrase that stayed with me and I can still hear it today as Freddie played it. Freddie was still going to Wilberforce College and playing with the orchestra. One night they had been playing for a dance somewhere and they found out Hayes was playing at a Road House that was on the highway they had to take to go back to Wilberforce, so they stopped at the…

So we played "Maytime" and I played the first few measures the way I heard Freddie play it and it pleased him so until he started calling me brother, and we called each other brother from then on, and the odd part about it, is that we did have similar resemblances in some certain degree.

The first time I ever shot dice was with Edgar Hayes and Lee Rainey. One morning after we had arrived in the city, someone suggested that we have a crap game and I joined the party although I did not know much about the game. We played tit for tat until Lee finally became broke or tired and went to bed. We were all playing in his flat. Edgar and I kept playing head and head until I finally broke him.
